classes.name: Estrogen — transdermal
classes.description: Transdermal 17β-estradiol (patch, gel, or spray); skips first-pass hepatic metabolism, lower VTE risk than oral.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen patch or gel absorbed through the skin — gentler on clot risk than pills.

classes.name: Estrogen — oral
classes.description: Oral estradiol or conjugated estrogens; effective, but first-pass hepatic metabolism raises VTE/clot and stroke risk vs transdermal.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen pill taken by mouth. Works well, but carries a higher clot risk than the patch.

classes.name: Progestogen
classes.description: Progestogen added to systemic estrogen for endometrial protection in patients with an intact uterus; micronized progesterone preferred.
classes.plainDescription: Added to estrogen if you still have a uterus, to protect the uterine lining.

classes.name: Vaginal (local) estrogen
classes.description: Low-dose vaginal estradiol (cream, tablet, insert, or ring) for genitourinary syndrome of menopause; minimal systemic absorption.
classes.plainDescription: Low-dose estrogen placed vaginally for dryness and urinary symptoms (GSM).

classes.name: Estrogen–progestin (oral combo)
classes.description: A single oral tablet with both an estrogen and a progestin, for a person with an intact uterus; generic estradiol/norethindrone acetate is the usual first-pass.
classes.plainDescription: One pill that combines estrogen and the uterus-protecting hormone.

records.verificationNote: Read directly off the Jan 1 2026 UHC Commercial PDL, 'Hormonal Agents - Hormone Replacement and Birth Control' section. 'estradiol transdermal patch weekly' is listed Tier 1 with annotation '(generic for Climara), QL' and no PA — the clean first-pass. 'estradiol patch twice weekly' is Tier 2 QL. Gels (Divigel/Estrogel/Elestrin) are Tier 3; Evamist spray Tier 2. Brand Climara/Vivelle-Dot/Minivelle carry the 'E' symbol (excluded/PA in CT, NJ, NY only — NOT applicable in North Carolina), so in NC they default to non-preferred brand status. QL applies; specific quantity not printed in PDL. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

records.verificationNote: Read directly off the Jan 1, 2026 UnitedHealthcare Commercial PDL (OptumRx-administered), 'Hormonal Agents - Hormone Replacement and Birth Control' section (p. 36). The row 'estradiol oral' is listed at Tier 1 with NO restriction symbol (no PA, no ST, no QL, no E) - it ships completely clean and is the unambiguous first-pass oral estrogen; this is generic estradiol tablet (0.5/1/2 mg), brand Estrace. Brand 'ESTRACE' (estradiol oral) is flagged with the 'E' symbol and shows no printed tier number, defaulting to non-preferred brand in North Carolina. 'PREMARIN ORAL' (conjugated estrogens, no generic) is Tier 3 (non-preferred brand). 'est estrogens-methyltest' / 'Estratest F.S.' (esterified estrogens-methyltestosterone) are Tier 1 but are estrogen+androgen combos rather than pure oral estrogens, so listed as borderline alternatives; 'ESTRATEST H.S.' is Tier 3. No generic conjugated estrogens, no Menest (esterified estrogens), and no estropipate lines appear in the document - those products are largely discontinued/unavailable in the US market and are not separately listed. KEY STATE NUANCE: the 'E' symbol legend reads 'May be excluded from coverage or subject to Prior Authorization in Connecticut, New Jersey and New York' - it does NOT apply in North Carolina; brand rows carry no separate printed tier. UnitedHealthcare publishes ONE national commercial PDL with state annotations; there is no MD-specific commercial PDF. boglActive is false - no brand is forced over the available generic estradiol tablet. CLINICAL CAVEAT (not a coverage fact): oral estrogen carries higher VTE/clot risk than transdermal. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

preferredAgent.sig: Take 200 mg by mouth at bedtime for 12 days each calendar month (sequential), or 100 mg by mouth at bedtime daily (continuous), alongside systemic estrogen for endometrial protection
preferredAgent.plainSig: Take this capsule at bedtime (it can make you drowsy). Either one capsule every night, or two capsules nightly for 12 days each month — follow whichever schedule your prescriber chose to protect your uterus.

alternatives.note: Tier 1, no PA — LOWER tier than micronized progesterone on this plan; the lowest-friction progestogen if cost is the priority

records.verificationNote: Read off the same PDL section. Generic 'progesterone oral' (micronized) is Tier 2 with NO PA — ships clean for endometrial protection, which is the stated goal. Note this plan places generic micronized progesterone at Tier 2 while generic 'medroxyprogesterone acetate oral' is Tier 1 (lower cost, also no PA). Brand Prometrium carries the 'E' symbol (excluded/PA only in CT, NJ, NY — not North Carolina) and no preferred tier number; brand Provera is Tier 4. Reported micronized progesterone as preferred first-pass because it is the clinically-preferred agent and ships without a PA round-trip; medroxyprogesterone (Tier 1) listed as the lower-friction-by-cost alternative. [Reused: same national UHC commercial PDL as the MD guide (2026-10-21); outside CT/NJ/NY its 'E' symbol means may be excluded]

Tiers/flags transcribed from extracted PDF text: mimvey Tier 1 (no flags); fyavolv Tier 1; jinteli Tier 1; estradiol-norethindrone acet Tier 2; amabelz Tier 2; ACTIVELLA Tier 4; BIJUVA Tier 3; PREMPHASE Tier 3; PREMPRO Tier 3.
